candidates.rationale: Current-epoch billing evidence consistently shows Photon-enabled DBU usage.
Low spill, queueing, and latency make one-size down a controlled canary candidate; absence of pressure is not proof of SLA safety.
The configured ceiling has not been used and queue pressure is low; tighten the guardrail without claiming direct savings.
Warehouse spends substantial time at minimum capacity without queue/scale pressure.
Idle-gap evidence supports a lower auto-stop target.
Serverless is evaluated as a separate migration experiment with a pre-canary DBU/AWS counterfactual and deterministic compatibility gate.

assumptions: Current configuration epoch is the decision baseline.
Forward DBU cost uses the deterministic current-epoch run-rate model.
AWS forward cost is modeled from observed current-epoch resource time and the configured regional price registry when available.

recommended_plan.decision_summary: Plan A — Optimize current warehouse type is the deterministic execution path; apply validation gates and regenerate after invalidating changes.

portfolio_economics.method: Stateful DBU+AWS bundle. Each step changes the evolving cost/resource state. Min-cluster and auto-stop remove remaining cluster-minutes rather than adding standalone savings; migration steps replace the state with a DBU+AWS pre-canary counterfactual. Downstream steps after invalidation must be regenerated after remeasurement.
